projects.impagency: Skills, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Department, Government of Maharashtra
projects.project_abstract: DAKSH Maharashtra supports the skills reform agenda in Maharashtra and aims to improve training and entrepreneurship for market-led employment. The Program is centered around 4 proposed results areas: (i) institutional strengthening for high-quality market-relevant training with robust MIS systems; (ii) improving the quality and market relevance of skill development programs at the training provider level; (iii) enhancing access for women and disadvantaged groups; and (iv) expanding skills training and entrepreneurship through private-public partnerships (PPPs).
projects.pdo: To improve skills and entrepreneurship training for enhanced employability in Maharashtra.

projects.project_name: Uttar Pradesh Knowledge-based Response to Schooling and Teaching
projects.impagency: Basic Education Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh
projects.project_abstract: The Program for Results (PforR) will support capacity-building of teachers; infrastructure strengthening and upgradation in select schools, and technology solutions for achieving the program outcomes. This operation will be supported by a Technical Assistance component that will use the Investment Project Financing (IPF) instrument to engage technical experts and organizations that can provide technical assistance, capacity building, and implementation support for the state’s nodal educational institutions - State Council of Education Research and Training (SCERT) and State Institute of Education Management and Training (SIEMAT), for several results areas. It will also be used for setting-up a Project Management Unit (PMU). The IPF component will not include any purchase of IT hardware, equipment, or servers by the state government or include support on aspects related to school infrastructure and facilities.
projects.pdo: To enhance quality in primary education and access to quality education and market relevant skills for secondary students and youthin Uttar Pradesh.

projects.project_name: Uttar Pradesh Clean Air Management Program
projects.impagency: Department of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change, State of Uttar Pradesh
projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Energy and Extractives,FY17 - Public Administration,FY17 - Transportation
projects.project_abstract: The proposed project uses  (a) a Program for Results (PforR) instrument for most of the program support, and (b) a technical assistance (TA) component using the Investment Project Financing (IPF) instrument. The PforR project would finance result achievements across three areas focused on (i) Strengthening State Capabilities for AQM planning and Operations; (ii) Sector measures for air pollution reductions; and (iii) IGP Airshed Cooperation.The program seeks to achieve 9 Disbursement Linked Indicators focused on achievement of:1) Airshed management decision support system in operation and use2) Increased human resource capacity for airshed management3) Number of households using clean cookstoves to meet cooking needs4) Number of hectares with increased fertilizer (nitrogen) use efficiency 5) Volume of animal manure, agriculture residue waste used for alternative productive uses and diverted from mismanagement and burning6) Number of brick kilns transitioned to improved air pollution control and resource efficiency technology7) Good practice models of improved urban mobility for clean air8) Number of heavy-duty vehicles (BS III or below) scrapped and taken off the road9) Common measures with other IGP statesThe IPF component will support the three result areas and achievement of the Program DLIs.
projects.pdo: To strengthen airshed management systems and improve air quality outcomes.

projects.project_name: India's Enhanced Health Service Delivery Program
projects.impagency: Department of Health and Family Welfare, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India,Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
projects.project_abstract: The development objective of India's Enhanced Health Service Delivery Program-for-Results (PforR) Project is to increase utilization of comprehensive primary health care services, improve quality of care, and strengthen governance of the health sector in India. The PforR Program will tackle reforms related to ensuring universal and effective health care coverage; spending more and better; and moving toward a system of accountability for results. The Program has three key result areas with a combination of technical interventions related to the provision of Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) and quality of care, and transversal interventions to strengthen governance and accountability. Those are: (i) strengthened service delivery through redesigned CPHC model; (ii) improved comprehensive quality of care; and (iii) transformed health sector governance, accountability, and institutional and management capacity. Seven priority states have been identified to be part of the Program based on the following factors: (i) leveraging WB state health systems operations to deepen impact; (ii) providing a mix of high-performing and not-so-well-performing states based on the NITI Aayog-MoHFW Annual State Health Index; (iii) ensuring geographical representation from all four regions of India; and (iv) providing opportunities for knowledge sharing and cross-learning based on state-specific CPHC initiatives. The Program will support interventions across the four universal actions recommended by the 2018 Lancet Global Health Commission on High Quality Health Systems in the Sustainable Development Goal Era (HQSS): redesigning service delivery, governing for quality, transforming the health workforce, and igniting demand for quality among citizens.
projects.pdo: To increase utilization of comprehensive primary health care services, improve quality of care, and strengthen governance of the health sector in India.

projects.impagency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying,National Dairy Development Board
projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Industry, Trade and Services
projects.project_abstract: The proposed project will address key gaps and deficiencies in the dairy sector in focus states in India and support the sector’s transformation towards increased productivity, resilience, and profitability. By doing so, it will contribute to key aspects of the GoI and the Bank’s CPF strategic objectives related to faster and broader agriculture sector growth and inclusive development. The project will also work closely with the pipeline project under development – Animal Health System Support for Improved One Health (AHSSOH) – to enhance animal health management. Farmers have limited access to the organized milk processing sector. Only about 36 percent of the marketable surplus is estimated to be sold to the organized sector. Small producers, who account for 70 percent of milk production, are particularly affected. Also, milk processed and marketed by the organized sector is safer and less likely to be contaminated, which offers health and food safety benefits. In addition to the marketing and food safety challenges Productivity is low mainly due to poor nutrition, health, the low genetic potential for milk production, and the near absence of well-run genetic improvement programs. Animal nutrition is undermined not only by feed and fodder scarcity but also lack of farmers‟ knowledge on how to better use existing feed resources. There is little extension advice available to farmers about improved animal feeding practices.The project will help to increase milk production by improving nutrition and enhancing farmers' knowledge on how to use better existing feed resources and optimal use of feed and fodder. This would be achieved through support to extensive training of dairy farmers and doorstep delivery of ration advisory services, integrated with veterinary support, together with convergence with the DAHD programme. The project will raise farmers' ‟awareness” about the importance of good quality milk and build their capacity for hygienic milk production, collection and sale. The collective sale will strengthen farmers‟ negotiating power and reduce transaction costs for such a highly perishable commodity.The project recognizes the role of an enabling policy and regulatory environment to support the intended investments. Consequently, project investments would be supported in those states that commit to certain time-bound actions onwards a more enabling policy environment.
projects.pdo: The project development objective is to enhance competitiveness, foster inclusion, improve resilience and reduce the carbon footprint of milk value chains, focusing on smallholder dairy farmers in project areas.

projects.project_name: Uttar Pradesh Agriculture Growth and Rural Enterprise Ecosystem Strengthening Project
projects.impagency: Uttar Pradesh Diversified Agriculture Support Project Society, Government of Uttar Pradesh
projects.major_sector_name: Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,Digital Development,Industry, Trade and Services
projects.project_abstract: The project will aim to: i) make investments market-led and orienting the agriculture and food system towards commercialization based on market intelligence;  ii) enhance the role of the private sector to drive innovation and investment in the sector and creating high quality jobs;  iii) enable smallholder farmers to benefit from improved access to technology and markets, thereby increasing farm incomes; and iv) utilize and build upon the institutional capacity existing in the state by developing strategic partnership to bring cutting edge technology to the sector.The project will promote productivity in smallholder agriculture, which is expected to intensify farming activity and may result in an increased use of fertilizers and pesticides by farmers as well as water. The project may also promote aquaculture and food processing activities. The project may support the procurement of small farm equipment for water lifting and crop drying, equipment to support fuel-efficient agro-logistics, and planting material. However, the project will not support the procurement of fertilizers and pesticides. Additionally, it has not yet been determined whether the project will support activities that may entail small-scale and localized construction or physical upgrades/improvements of aggregation facilities, warehouses, and cold storage.
projects.pdo: To increase farmers' income through improved crop productivity, climate resilience, and commercialization of agrifood systems in Selected Regions of Uttar Pradesh.

projects.project_name: Kerala Climate Resilient Agri- Value Chain Modernization (KERA) Project
projects.impagency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Kerala
projects.major_sector_name: Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,Industry, Trade and Services
projects.project_abstract: The project aims to address the main challenges hindering Kerala’s agriculture food system transition as part of the State's continued structural transformation. It will focus on addressing three main themes: (i) promoting resilience to climate change and contributing to India's mitigation targets; (ii) enhancing smallholder commercialization for value addition; and (iii) strengthening the private sector's role within the food system, especially MSMEs. Project interventions in these three main areas will focus on: (i) supporting resilience and adaptation through strengthening the extension system to promote an improved package of practices of climate smart agricultural technologies relevant to specific agroecological conditions (including integrated pest management to respond to changing disease vectors), and delivering climate change mitigation results by focusing on reducing emissions in paddy production, primarily through the adoption of alternative wet and dry (AWD) production techniques, as well as measures to improve fertilizer efficiency and other opportunities to promote the decarbonization of value chains including energy efficient storage facilities; (ii) facilitating productive alliances between small-holder farmers (individually or more likely via farmer producer companies [FPCs] to promote value addition and diversification into higher-value crop production, providing on-farm or community-level value chain infrastructure such as storage facilities and equipment to promote value addition, and support to farmer organizations, etc; and (iii) providing training and partial grants to existing MSMEs as part of a coherent and targeted hand-holding service, support to relevant agri-tech start-ups, and support to food/ agri-parks of various sizes to facilitate the clustering of competitive agro-processing.Project activities entail a mix of technical assistance type of support in the form of promotion and demonstration of new technologies including high-yield varieties and diversification into high-value commodities, as well as small-scale irrigation practices to enhance access to water and efficient use. It may support the provision of input packages directly such as seeds and will provide technical assistance to link farmers with input markets. The project will work with established FPCs to help them increase their capacity for aggregation, value addition and business management. Project activities may entail physical upgrades/ improvements to localized and small-scale irrigation systems, facilities for hygiene and waste management, and existing aggregation facilities (local farmer markets), including potential construction of warehouses and cold storage depending on the need and feasibility, and without requiring land acquisition. The project will also promote productivity in smallholder agriculture, which is expected to intensify farming activity, which would increase water usage and may result in an increased (albeit more efficient) use of fertilizers and pesticides by farmers. However, the project will not finance the purchase of inputs such as these. The project will provide technical assistance to existing agriculture and food sector MSMEs and small-scale agri parks, and also support an initial feasibility study for a new large-scale agri-park. Technical assistance to small-scale agri parks may also entail small-scale and localized physical upgrades/ improvements and construction on existing agri-park parcels. The project will also leverage commercial financing for plantations and smallholders, through the establishment of a Partial Risk Guarantee. The project will also support the ongoing reconfiguration of the DoA’s institutional structure and help strengthen coordination among key program and service delivery agencies with a goal of delivering agriculture support services effectively and efficiently. Project activities will primarily entail capacity building including procurement and use of digital technologies for advisory information dissemination as well as equipment and goods to facilitate mobility of extension workers to reach remote areas. Additionally, the project will also support development of new mechanisms for land consolidation through increased collective decision-making supported by policy and institutional measures to support land leasing.
projects.pdo: To promote the resilience and commercialization of Kerala’s food and agriculture sector.

projects.impagency: Department of Tribal Welfare, Government of Tripura

projects.project_abstract: The development objective of the Tripura Rural Economic Growth and Service Delivery Project for India is to enhance connectivity and access to improved services and economic opportunities for tribal areas in Tripura. The project comprises of four components. The first component, strengthening foundations for economic development will support strengthening the foundations for economic development in the tribal blocks through an integrated set of investments in agricultural livelihoods and rural roads that can both ease access to markets and to schools. The second component, investing in services to develop human capital will support investments to increase the average years of educational attainment and enhanced preparedness for labor market transitions for students in the twenty-three (23) tribal blocks and especially in the twelve (12) priority tribal blocks. The third component, strengthening institutional capacities for service delivery objective is to support the strengthening of local institutions in the tribal blocks for improved service delivery. The fourth component, contingent emergency response component will support the provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.

projects.impagency: Public Works Roads Department, Government of Assam
projects.project_abstract: The PforR Program’s boundary is restricted to improving bridges on the rural roads network – “rural bridges”. The Program interventions include: (a) maintenance; (b) widening single lane bridges; (c) replacement of temporary, distressed and collapsed/washed out bridges, and construction of new bridges; and (d) updating Electric Vehicle Policy to enhance rural e- mobility & establishing Green Rural Freight and Public Transportation Hubs along the rural roads network. The Program supports extensive resilience and institutional building initiatives with four process DLIs, including (e) enhancing resilience of bridges; (f) strengthening Environmental and Social management capability; (g) strengthening APWRD’s financial and procurement capability; and (h) strengthening roads and bridges management capability. IPF Component (TA Component) includes:a)	Prepare Program rural bridges investment and manage Program implementation, including Detail Project Report (DPR), Construction Supervision Consultants (CSC), Transport hub design, GRS, Gender Action Plan, and E&S impact managementb)	Program management support, studies, and system upgrading including Independent Verification Agent, Program Management Consultant, Technical Audit Consultant, Individual Consultants, Impact evaluation, training, road financing strategy, systems upgrading/development, studies; and administrative, legal, and operating expenses.c)	Strengthen the Assam Road Research and Training Institute (ARRTI) - center of excellence-, including training material development, delivering induction training and short-term courses, and research. This TA component is designed to achieve Disbursement Linked Indicator (DLI) #1 and the Program Action Plan (PAP) on environment and social risk management included in the PforR Operation. This is to address the gaps identified by the Environmental and Social Systems Assessment (ESSA) undertaken to assess the country systems and capacity of Institutions to effectively manage E&S risks. The DLI #1 covers:(i)	Adoption of Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) and Environmental and Social Policy - Indigenous People Policy (ESP-IPP)  that aligns with country laws and good international industry practices (GIIP) [The ESP-IPP and RPF including improved systems and procedures supported by the PforR will subsequently apply to the whole of government’s program. The ESP-IPP/RPF will include the screening criteria to avoid financing of any High E&S risk subprojects under Bank’s Program]; (ii)	Setting up of a dedicated E&S management unit that will report to planning and finance wings of the APWRD; and (iii)	Establishment of digital system to track compliance of the policies on real time basis. The DLI#1 is incentivized with a total sum of US$ 4.8 million (Scalable).The PAP is designed to ensure that civil works are initiated only after the client provides encumbrance free land in accordance with the ESP-IPP and RPF to the contractors before the commencement of the works. Both the DLI and PAP will be adopted sector wide by the Department. The Verification Agency will be expected to follow the verification protocol to the compliance of the PAP and the DLI. The TA component will support the (i) preparation of sub-project level ESIAs/ESMPs in accordance with the APWRD’s ESP-IPP that aligns with the national/state legal policy requirements and international standards, including the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) supported by PforR; (ii) set up the Grievance Management Systems; (iii) develop and implement the capacity building program of APWRD by the ESMU; (iv) prepare the Gender Action Plan; (v) implement the systems for evidence based monitoring for evidence based reporting supported under the PforR.
projects.pdo: The program development objective (PDO) is to build green, inclusive, and resilient connectivity in rural Assam and strengthen the Assam Public Works Roads Department’s roads and bridges management capability.

projects.project_name: Meghalaya Multisectoral Project for Adolescent Wellbeing, Empowerment and Resilience (MPOWER)
projects.impagency: Government of Meghalaya
projects.project_abstract: The goal of the program is to promote the well-being and empowerment of adolescents and to strengthen their productivity and resilience so that they can contribute fully to the sustainable economic growth of the state. The program will strengthen the capability of the State of Meghalaya to empower adolescent boys and girls, aged 9 to 19, through multi-sectoral interventions (education/skills/counselling) that can strengthen their human capital, and support their transition from school to productive work. The program would support strengthening adolescents' life skills, physical and reproductive health, and career aspirations.Component 1.  Learning Mission, Life Skills, and Career Preparation in Schools: This component will focus on improving human capital outcomes for adolescents in upper primary (grades 6-8), secondary (grades 9-10), and higher secondary (grades 11-12) government and government-aided schools in the state. Component 2: Community Interventions and pathways for out-of-school adolescents: This component will focus on improving human capital outcomes for out of school adolescents and creating an enabling environment for them through active engagement and capability building of their parents, community members, and frontline workers. It will also support setting up of a “Hub and Spoke Model” of community-based service delivery through the network of Community Clubs (located at the level of cluster of villages) and Youth Centres (located at Block levels). Component 3: State Capability and Program Management: This component will focus on strengthening the institutional capacity of the state for improved coordination, governance, and outreach, set up Youth Centres as Block level hubs for adolescents and youth, and support improved management of data, and day to operation and management of the project. This component will also support adolescent girls in completing the secondary education cycle through academic counselling, development of a multisectoral competency and wellbeing framework, and facilitating safe spaces for young girls. Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC): This component will support an immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.
projects.pdo: To enhance multi-sectoral service delivery and capability of the State of Meghalaya to improve adolescents' human capital outcomes.

projects.impagency: Rural Development and Panchayat Department, Government of Karnataka,Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department, Government of Karnataka

projects.pdo: To increase access to safely managed drinking water and strengthen institutions for sustainable rural water service delivery in Karnataka.

projects.project_name: Electric Vehicle Operations and Lending for a Vibrant Ecosystem
projects.borrower: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
projects.impagency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Energy and Extractives,FY17 - Information and Communications Technologies,FY17 - Transportation
projects.project_abstract: The development objective of the Electric Vehicle Operations and Lending for a Vibrant Ecosystem (EVOLVE) is to foster the transition to sustainable electric vehicles in the two and three-wheeler segments. The Project will take a three-pronged approach to address current challenges. First, it will address the key market failure underlying the lack of access to affordable commercial financing for e-2/3Ws and associated charging infrastructure through a risk-sharing program (RSP), which will offer credit-enhancement and on-lending products to a diverse range of participating financial institutions (PFIs). End borrowers are expected to include, inter alia, micro, small and medium enterprises, leasing companies, fleet operators, aggregators, and charging-as-a-service (“CaaS”) and battery-as-a-service (“BaaS”) businesses. Micro enterprises include individual, driver cum owners with mandatory Udyam Aadhar registration, a unique registration mechanism for MSMEs. PFIs will offer reduced interest cost and lend more actively to women borrowers. EVOLVE will systematically embed and test de-risking measures to improve the ability of the PFIs to appraise and price risks, and build a track record in e-2/3W lending, thereby moving towards a self-sustaining EV financing ecosystem. Second, EVOLVE will contribute to addressing barriers and fostering key enablers by leveraging the large-scale data generated from the EVs financed under EVOLVE RSP to help policy makers in framing the EV transition, help consumers make informed decisions about switching to EVs, and mitigate lenders’ concerns over lending to EVs, and by building the capacity of the Program Manager and PFIs. EVOLVE will also contribute to the knowledge base in key areas of sustainability such as RE integration, effective lifecycle management of batteries, and facilitation of women’s access to financing to promote vehicle ownership, and women’s labor force participation associated with e-2/3Ws. Lastly, EVOLVE will provide the scale necessary to make the aggregation of carbon credits viable, which could monetize GHG emissions reductions, a key positive externality of EVs. EVOLVE would be designed with an open architecture, to allow other financing agencies and donors with specific interests to benefit from its structure. SIDBI, a pan-India financial institution, will perform the role of ‘Program Manager’ at the national level, and establish and implement the EVOLVE RSP.
projects.pdo: The project development objective is to foster the transition to sustainable electric two- and three-wheelers

projects.project_name: Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST) Project

projects.project_abstract: The development objective of the Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST) Project for India is to strengthen management capacity, access to, and quality of the secondary healthcare system in Assam. The project comprises of three components. The first component, strengthened management capacity of health systems at state, district, and facility level consists of following sub-components: (i) internal performance agreements (IPAs) to strengthen management capacity; and (ii) technical support and project operating costs to strengthen management capacity. The second component is improved access to and quality of essential services in existing secondary facilities. The third component, enhanced access to and structural quality of secondary care will invest in: (a) upgrading up to 10 community health center (CHCs) and sub-district hospitals (SDHs) to district hospital (DH) following national guidelines and provision of medical equipment and goods to enhance equitable access to secondary care, and (b) incremental operating costs of these newly upgraded facilities to improve structural quality of secondary care.
projects.pdo: To strengthen management capacity, access to, and quality of the secondary healthcare system in Assam.

projects.project_name: Uttarakhand Climate Responsive Rainfed Farming Project

projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Industry, Trade and Services
projects.project_abstract: The project will work towards (i) reduction of net GHG emission relative to control villages with similar cropping pattern; (ii) achievement of resilience of production systems by adopting precision-farming techniques; and (iii) increased profitability through enhanced productivity, reduced cost of cultivation, and additional income through carbon credits. An integrated digital platform for evidence-based decision-making will support the project activities. The project will focus on small and marginal farmers, including women farmers, and landless households. The project will be implemented in 1,226 villages covering a catchment area of 243,418 hectares (ha), which includes arable and non-arable land.
projects.pdo: Improve production system resilience to make mountain farming emission competitive and profitable in selected micro-watersheds of Uttarakhand

projects.project_name: Enhancing Landscape and Ecosystem Management - Tripura
projects.impagency: Forest department, Government of Tripura
projects.project_abstract: The proposed project aims to improve landscape management to enhance ecosystem services and economic benefits for the forest-dependent communities in Tripura. More specifically, the project will strengthen the capacities of the state government and local actors to restore forest landscapes by introducing a landscape approach and helping utilize technological solutions. Through the proposed project, the degraded forest landscapes will be restored by implementing community-led integrated forest landscape and natural resource management plans in the selected areas in support of improved ecosystem services, such as water availability, soil conservation, and wildlife habitat protection, among others. The improved forest ecosystem will contribute to increased carbon sequestration and climate resilience and adaptive capacities of the communities. The project also aims at creating sustainable forest-based and NTFP livelihoods by facilitating value chain improvement and market linkages. As a direct contribution to income generating opportunities, the project will forge new employment avenues such as and strengthening existing and supporting the establishment of new value chains for NTFPs and HVFPs such as Bamboo and Agarwood, and ecotourism/nature-based tourism. For enhancing NTFP market linkages, the project will conduct training and capacity building for the collection and producer groups, forest institutions, NTFP traders, MSMEs, etc. and organize events to bring buyers and sellers together. Finally, the project will strengthen the functional and technical capacities of state institutions for improved landscape governance and disaster risk prevention by introducing new technology on forest monitoring and value chain management, while facilitating collaborative landscape management with the local actors. Other interventions aimed at the inclusion of tribal population, gender empowerment, and vocational development for women and youth will be prioritized during project preparation and implementation.
projects.pdo: The project development objective is to improve landscape management and increase environmental and economic benefits for targeted forest dependent communities in Tripura,

projects.impagency: National Disaster Management Authority
projects.project_abstract: The proposed National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project Phase III will, while partly continuing the cyclone preparedness and emergency management agenda targeted under phases I and II, shift the program’s focus from life-saving interventions to systemic resilience to disasters and extreme events amidst increasing climatic changes. NCRMP III will serve as a knowledge project by developing the analytical underpinnings to better understand and inform future efforts to enhance systemic resilience to climate change in coastal areas. First, the project will establish a knowledge platform on coastal resilience to integrate ongoing approaches and experiences and identify missing pieces of the agenda, with a focus on potential climate impacts. This platform will enable joint learning across coastal states and benchmarking of global best practices and lessons learned from Bank projects. Second, the project will analyze important biophysical and socioeconomic trends to provide empirical evidence on priority interventions and investments for next-generation coastal resilience. Third, the project will undertake action-oriented analytics in themes emerging from the experience of NCRMP II. Within a select number of low-lying coastal cities, the project will develop master drainage plans to address current and future drainage needs in light of amplified urban flooding risks posed by climate change. The project will assess saline embankments in coastal India to enable the development of a raised and strengthened embankment system to withstand the impact of cyclones. Lastly, the project will identify the most critical and exposed critical infrastructure assets, with a focus on power sector and lightning risk mitigation needs, as candidates for the strengthening of infrastructure to catalyze long-term growth and enhance the adaptive capacity of coastal communities to climate change and sea level rise.
projects.pdo: The Project Development Objective is to reduce vulnerability of coastal communities to cyclone and other hydro-meteorological hazards in the target states and enhance the knowledge base for systemic coastal resilience.

projects.project_name: Uttarakhand Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Project
projects.impagency: Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority, Government of Uttarakhand
projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Public Administration,FY17 - Transportation
projects.project_abstract: The objective of the Uttarakhand Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Project for India is to enhance the climate and disaster resilience of critical public infrastructure and strengthen disaster risk management capacity in Uttarakhand. The project has five components. (1) Enhancing Infrastructure Resilience component will support the development of climate- and disaster-resilient priority infrastructure and integrate resilience into infrastructure planning. (2) Improving Emergency Preparedness and Response component will support improving the capabilities of Uttarakhand’s government entities and first responders to predict, prepare for, and respond to disasters. (3) Preventing and Managing Forest and General Fires component will support enhancing the capacity of the Uttarakhand government and local communities to prevent and manage forest and general fires. (4)  Project Management component will support project management and knowledge sharing. (5) Contingent Emergency Response Component component will allow provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed, through the reallocation of undisbursed loan proceeds.
projects.pdo: To enhance the climate and disaster resilience of select critical public infrastructure in Uttarakhand and strengthen the capacity of the State Government to respond to emergencies, including fires.

projects.project_name: Enhancing Landscape and Ecosystem Management (ELEMENT) Project
projects.impagency: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER),Society for Climate Resilient Agriculture in Nagaland (SoCRAN),Government of Nagaland,State Forest Development Agency (SFDA), Department of Forests ,Government of Tripura
projects.project_abstract: The objective of the Enhancing Landscape and Ecosystem Management (ELEMENT) Project for India is to improve landscape management and increase benefits for targeted forest dependent communities in Tripura and Nagaland. There are five components to the project, the first component being strengthening capacities for integrated landscape management. This component includes four subcomponents: strengthening the capacity of participating states relevant institutions in participatory planning, implementation, and monitoring; strengthening capacity of participating states institutions for Research and Development (R&D) and value chain development; Strengthening the capacity of existing and new community institutions for decentralized natural resources management; and knowledge and information sharing on innovation. The second component is the restoring landscapes for improved ecosystem services. This component includes two subcomponents: developing community landscape management plans, and implementation of community landscape management plans in targeted catchments. The third component is the enhancing landscape-based value-chains for economic transformation. This component includes two subcomponents: agroforestry, forestry, and NTFP in value chain development and forest landscape enterprises and augmenting eco-tourism opportunities. The fourth component is the project management, monitoring, and evaluation.  Finally, the fifth component is the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC). Provision of immediate response to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, as needed. This will include reallocation of loan proceeds from other components to provide immediate response (which may include recovery and reconstruction support) following an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.
projects.pdo: Improve landscape management and increase benefits for targeted forest dependent communities in Tripura and Nagaland.

projects.project_name: Assam Disaster Resilient Hill Roads Development Project
projects.impagency: Public Works Department (Roads) EAP
projects.project_abstract: The proposed operation will support: (i) reconstruction, rehabilitation, improvement of selected climate-resilient hill  roads in Dima Hasao, Karbi Anglong, and west Karbi Anglong districts; (ii) developing agricultural supply chain for a cluster of roadside tribal communities and promoting market-driven and climate-resilient agriculture; (iii) developing green and efficient rural freight and public transportation system; and (iv) building multi-modal transport network resilience and early warning system. The hill roads project will integrate the tribal communities with the economy of Assam and the sub region by  improving the resilience of road connectivity and the efficiency of the agricultural and  women tribal community households textile and handicraft producers supply chain. The project will also develop resilience enhancing instruments, establish early warning system (EWS) and emergency response system during disaster events, and strengthen institutional capacity to manage disaster prone roads.
projects.pdo: The overarching goal for the Assam transportation sector support is to “provide green transportation and climate resilient roads and bridges infrastructure and integrate smallholding farmers and tribal communities in Assam with the Southeast and South Asian markets.”  The overarching goal will be achieved by implementing a Series of Operations (SOPs). SOP 1: The  PDO for the Assam Resilient Rural Bridges Program (P178581), approved on March 2, 2024 is to build green, inclusive, and resilient connectivity in rural Assam and strengthen the Assam Public Works Roads Department’s roads and bridges management capability. SOP 2: The PDO for the proposed Assam Disaster Resilient Hill Roads Development Project (P180672) is to enhance climate disaster resilience of hill roads and promote green and inclusive market access in selected hill areas of Assam.

projects.project_name: Tamil Nadu Women Employment and Safety (TN WESAFE) Operation
projects.impagency: Special Program Implementation Department.
projects.project_abstract: The Government of Tamil Nadu (GoTN) implements a multi-sector program that focuses on women’s economic empowerment through skill building, enterprise support, infrastructure development, and service delivery interventions. Complementing the state’s economic vision, the Tamil Nadu Women’s Policy (2021, draft) puts forward a comprehensive plan for women’s empowerment. The proposed PforR Program, Tamil Nadu Women Employment and Safety (WeSafe) will support a subset of the government program to improve women’s access to quality jobs in non-farm and emerging sectors. Traditional government programming on women’s employment has adopted a sector-specific delivery approach; either through skill development, rural livelihoods, entrepreneurship promotion, or school-to-work transition related interventions. The WeSafe Program proposes an alternate, integrated programming approach to address bottlenecks that impede women’s access to quality jobs through: (i) strengthening state-level planning capacities via the state-led platform on women’s employment and district-led women’s quality employment plans; (ii) promoting targeted skilling and entrepreneurship support linked to emerging sectors; and (iii) improving delivery of enabling services in women’s safety, affordable housing, and care.The Program will support three Result Areas (RAs) that will contribute towards the achievement of the Program Development Objective.1.	RA 1: EMPLOY: Improved labor market performance for women in emerging sectors: Result Area 1 introduces an outcome-driven approach to enhance the relevance, accessibility, quality, and efficiency of skills training and entrepreneurship support for women in Tamil Nadu.2.	RA 2: ENABLE: Enhanced delivery of enabling services to promote women’s employment: Under Results Area 2, the Program will support setting up an investment framework to improve coordinated outreach, quality, and impact of enabling services particularly safety/violence prevention in public places and workplaces, affordable housing options, and care services.3.	RA 3: EMPOWER: Strengthened state capacities, technical partnerships, and institutional structures for women’s employment: Under Results Area 3, the state will develop a common results framework to support the roll-out of the state’s women policy and directly contribute to the state’s economic goal of achieving a trillion-dollar economic status. The Program will support setting-up of a state-led platform for women’s employment.
projects.pdo: The Program Development Objective is to improve women's access to quality jobs in non-farm sectors.

projects.project_name: Strengthening Coastal Resilience and the Economy Project
projects.impagency: Department of Environment, Climate Change, and Forests, State of Tamil Nadu,Department of Forest, Ecology, and Environment, State of Karnataka
projects.project_abstract: The SHORE MPA program will support India’s vision for Integrated Coastal Zone Management while ensuring that the coastal zone's environment, landscapes, and natural values are in harmony with economic development. This will be done through convergence between federal and state governments based on their coastal priorities. Many coastal issues – particularly those related to local adaptation capacity, water resources, and infrastructure management – have regional dimensions, especially given the geographic and economic interconnectedness of coastal States. Under Phase-1 of the SHORE MPA, the coastal States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu will be supported through shared learning and developing cost-effective solutions to build resilience to natural disasters and climate change. The project will provide positive environment benefits and will minimize exposure of people and economic assets to potential damage due to the effects of climate, through integrated planning and promotion of community driven nature-based solutions. The PDO will be achieved through four components that focus on: (i) stronger local institutions for integrated management of coastal zones; (ii) resilient shorelines through long-term planning and measures for protection of physical and natural assets and biodiversity conservation; (iii) resilient communities through income diversification, jobs and improved livelihood opportunities, specifically for vulnerable groups including women; and iv) healthier coastal ecosystems through measures for reducing plastic pollution and promoting circularity. The project primarily involves the following four categories of interventions: i) soft nature-based interventions for coastal erosion management,  e.g mangrove afforestation, bio shields, sea grass, shelter belts, ecotourism measures such as board walks, blue flag beaches; ii) small scale works that e.g. Turtle and Dugong conservation centres, erosion management in one small island; prevention of ocean bound plastic pollution though establishment of trash barriers, traps and nets, small scale plastic collection/ segregation centres and material recovery facilities; iii) Goods primarily involving procurement e.g. equipment such as boats, water quality monitoring equipment, cameras, drones, etc.; iv) awareness initiatives, such as signages, sensitization programmes through SHGs (Plastic Mitras), festivals, etc., and; v)  services involving various consultancies e.g. study on plastic pollution abatement, carbon finance approaches, etc.
projects.pdo: To increase coastal protection and conservation, enhance livelihood benefits, and reduce marine plastic pollution in targeted coastal communities.

projects.project_name: Gurugram Metro Huda to Cyber City, Haryana
projects.impagency: Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL)
projects.project_abstract: Component 1: Investments in an accessible and sustainable Metrorail system. This component will finance: a) Metro rail infrastructure. Construction of approximately 28.50 km of elevated metro line in Gurugram, with 27 metro stations, depot, procurement & installation of rolling stock, electric, telecommunication, signaling, and control systems;  b) Multi-modal integration with other public transit systems; and c) Infrastructure for first and last mile connectivity including bus routing, bike sharing facilities and improvement in public spaces. Component 2: Promoting Transit Oriented Development (TOD) and integrated urban development in the catchment area of the metro line. This component will finance: a) Technical assistance to policies, planning and regulatory framework for TOD and integrated urban development strategy. b) Identification of prioritized resilient infrastructure in the catchment area for investment planning; and c) Pilot TOD complex development at/around two selected stations including planning, design, and implementation.Component 3: Technical assistance and capacity building to the key transport and urban development institutions. This component will finance: a) Technical support to inclusive and green infrastructure planning and design;b) Analytical activities for identification of innovative financing instruments for the metro system; c) Technical assistance for citizen engagement and gender inclusion; andd) Project management and operation.
projects.pdo: The PDO is to improve transit accessibility of Gurugram Metropolitan Area and promote integrated urban development around selected stations area.

projects.project_name: Second Low-Carbon Energy Programmatic Development Policy Financing
projects.impagency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
projects.major_sector_name: FY17 - Energy and Extractives,FY17 - Industry, Trade and Services
projects.project_abstract: India has made very significant development progress in recent decades and is expected to remain on an ascendent trajectory: its aspirations to become a high-income economy by 2047 would require it to elevate its rate of growth even further. From 1991 to today, the size of the economy has multiplied more than ten times, and gross domestic product (GDP) per capita seven times. From 1993-2022, the extreme poverty rate declined from 48 percent to 12.9 percent, reducing the number of extreme poor people by about 262 million. India’s past achievements set the tone for its future ambitions, notably the target to reach high income by 2047, which will require the economy to grow at 8 percent per annum on average over the next two decades. The actions supported under the proposed operation reflect India’s resolute and pragmatic approach to addressing climate change challenges. India’s policymakers are attempting to strike a complex balance between multiple objectives that entail inherent tradeoffs: boosting growth and innovation, including through targeted industrial policies; achieving energy security; and, contributing to global climate change objectives. Providing secure and affordable energy supply is a top priority for the GoI, with coal remaining the cheapest baseload supply available. The GoI’s drive to promote domestic manufacturing through “Make in India” will boost domestic productive capacity in RE, but it pushes up RE costs in the short-to-medium term, potentially delaying the large-scale adoption of RE. India’s policymakers are also trying to maximize the leveraging of public spending to crowd in the private sector and domestic commercial financing resources by providing just enough support to elicit private sector interest and drive down the cost curves, while optimizing the use of public resources.
projects.pdo: To accelerate the development of low-carbon energy in India.

projects.project_abstract: The proposed Surat Resilience Enhancement Project (SREP) is expected to support the Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) and the Tapi River Front Development Corporation Limited (TRFDCL) in implementing the Tapi Riverfront Rejuvenation Plan (TRRP) within the broader context of mainstreaming resilience in municipal operations and increasing resilience of the city to extreme flood and heat events, ensuring sustainability of resilient infrastructure development through leverage of own source revenues including land value capture mechanisms, achieving economic rejuvenation of the riverfront area, and integrating nature-based and green infrastructure solutions into the riverfront development. The TRRP is seeking to bend the curve by taking a resilience approach to riverfront development instead of a simple placemaking approach which is common to riverfront development projects in India. SMC is updating its draft conceptual master plan for the TRRP spread along 33.6 km on each side of Tapi river between the Kathore Bridge to a proposed barrage downstream of Singanpore wier. TRRP is expected to construct new embankments where required as well as inspect and strengthen existing embankments and dykes on the riverfront while making space available for increased economic, recreational and cultural activities. These activities are proposed to be implemented in two phases: Phase I, an up to10 km river stretch along both banks between the proposed barrage (connecting Rundh and Bhata) and the Singanpore weir; and Phase II, the remaining 23.6 km river stretch along both banks upstream from the Singanpore weir to the Kathore bridge. Through these interventions, the SMC expects to reduce the city’s flooding risks and beautify the cityscape to induce recreational, tourism and commercial activities, as well as prevent saltwater intrusion through the construction of the proposed Barrage (to be financed by SMC separately, i.e. non-World Bank financing). The proposed SREP Project will implement Phase I of the TRRP, and intends to set the technical, quality, legal, aesthetic, and E&S practices benchmarks for the following phase to follow, whether or not this is financed by the World Bank.The SREP will bring in international good practices in urban riverfront development and resilient infrastructure service delivery including: (i) interventions needed to make “room for the river”, while ensuring the livelihood of residents; (ii) incorporating shared spaces along the riverbanks for the river and for people, guided by ecological thinking; (iii) an inclusive development approach with proactive and continuous stakeholder engagement to define the multiple uses of spaces; as well as (iv) a sustainable financial and operational model to help the SMC, including through TRFDCL, manage its infrastructure assets and sustain effective and efficient service delivery in the long run. Public spaces along the river will be treated as a city public good and will get a careful, site and community specific programming and participatory design, that attends to city needs and cultural practices. The output of the investments will not only enhance the flood risk management capacity of the city and improve the living conditions of the residents, but also enhance economic development opportunities for both the public and the private sectors.The SREP suggests interventions under three complementary pillars. The 'resilience pillar' focuses on delivery of the TRRP as explained above. The 'institutions pillar' focuses on institutionalizing climate resilience actions in SMC including assigning one of the existing special implementation units called 'Cells' in SMC as the 'Climate Action Unit' (CAU) for quality assurance of all large investment projects and sectoral strategies and coordinating all climate resilience related matters. The CAU will serve as the anchor and nerve center for advancing SMC’s ambition of becoming the first ‘Green Municipal Corporation’ of India. The 'finance pillar' focuses on strengthening the investment planning and financial management systems, upgrading existing asset management MIS, upgrading procedures for disposition of monetizable assets, supporting SMC in undertaking pilot land monetization transactions especially focusing on land parcels falling within the TRRP, strengthening systems and procedures for management of unused and underused real estate, and building SMC’s technical capacity to manage the new real estate portfolio management system, in addition to looking at avenues for leveraging other land value capture tools through strengthening of real estate-based fees and policies including floor space index (FSI) and transferrable development rights (TDR). The three pillars will be supplemented by project management support and capacity augmentation. The four proposed components of SREP will be: Component 1: Resilient Urban Infrastructure Investments- C1.1: Tapi riverfront development investments proposed in Phase I of the TRRP, including: (i) flood risk control and resilience enhancement through a combination of green infrastructure (nature-based solutions) and grey infrastructure (engineered solutions and embankments) to arrive at a solution that achieves a harmonious balance between interventions on flood protection, urban ecology and urban riverfront amenity provision; (ii) public space enhancement and land redevelopment to increase the amenities and economic opportunities for the residents and business owners along the riverfront; and (iii) enhancement of cultural heritage assets and infrastructure along the riverfront that promote cultural tourism.- C1.2: Select supplementary resilient infrastructure investments, including a drainage interceptor project to rehabilitate the drainage outfall system along Tapi river, and small additional essential investments not proposed under TRRP such as access roads/mobility, etc. Component 2: Institutional Strengthening on Resilience Planning - C1.1: Institutional resilience and climate mainstreaming including setting-up and operationalization of the Climate Action Unit which would lead mainstreaming of climate and resilience actions in SMC including through translation of the existing second-generation climate strategy into a costed Climate Action Plan (CAP), mainstreaming disaster and climate resilience in all large projects of SMC, initiating green budgeting, setting up green accounting codes, exploring green financing through green municipal bonds and PPPs, fostering inter- and intra-departmental coordination, capacity building of SMC staff, developing a one-city one-map approach that ensures coordination between all developmental projects of SMC, among others. - C1.2: Operationalizing an integrated multi-hazard early warning system (EWS) and emergency response system (ERS) including modernization of the Hydromet monitoring network, including the development of a concept of operation (CONOPS) for key stakeholders, modernization in current EWS and ERS towards feeding into development of a multi-hazard EWS and ERS defining the development of a hydrological-hydraulic model for the forecasting, guidance and dissemination on flood warning in Surat as well as other hazards such as urban heat, vector borne pandemics, etc., integration with SMC's Command and Control Center (CCC) towards possible hosting of the integrated multi-hazard EWS and ERS, improve early warning dissemination systems, capacity building of SMC for disaster preparedness and response, among others. Component 3: Municipal Finance Improvement - C3.1: Enhancing overall performance on municipal finance of SMC, including technical assistance to help the SMC improve its capacity, systems, and practices in financial management, including towards integrating climate strategies, plans, and policies in fiscal and public financial management, as well as climate budget tagging for resilient urban development investments.- C2.2: Improving revenue performance of the SMC, thr

projects.project_name: Bihar Water Security and Irrigation Modernization Project
projects.impagency: Water Resources Department (WRD), Government of Bihar
projects.major_sector_name: Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,Public Administration,Water, Sanitation and Waste Management
projects.project_abstract: Bihar, despite its fertile lands in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, faces significant challenges in water management, with inconsistent monsoons, inadequate irrigation, frequent flooding, and drought severely limiting agricultural productivity and economic growth. This project aims to address these issues through two key interventions: improving irrigation systems and enhancing flood and erosion control. Using Investment Project Financing (IPF) and Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), the project seeks to transform Bihar’s water management sector and ensure long-term sustainability.The project comprises four components, addressing both environmental and social concerns. Component 1 focuses on restoring and modernizing irrigation infrastructure without disturbing the river’s main stem or the flow in the river. This will optimize water availability, reduce losses, and promote efficient water use, supporting climate-resilient agriculture. Component 2 tackles flood risk reduction by strengthening existing embankments. The project will not finance the construction of new embankments, instead observed damages in stretches of embankments and riverbanks that are affecting the protection of canal infrastructure, and the command irrigation area will be strengthened. This approach minimizes environmental disruption while protecting communities and irrigation infrastructure from future flood and drought risks. The project will also explore green infrastructure such as nature-based solutions.Component 3 strengthens water governance and institutional frameworks by implementing operational procedures, testing new irrigation service models, and expanding early warning systems for floods and droughts. Component 4 ensures effective project execution through monitoring and evaluation, integrating climate co-benefits, gender inclusivity, and citizen engagement. The project aligns with World Bank policies, addressing potential social impacts, such as the presence of squatters, while promoting equitable and sustainable outcomes. Together, these interventions aim to modernize Bihar’s water management, enhancing agricultural productivity and community resilience.
projects.pdo: To improve irrigation services and enhance flood resilience in Bihar.

projects.impagency: Assam Public Works (Roads) Department, EAP
projects.project_abstract: The project focuses on upgrading 360 km of damaged roads with climate-resilient features to mitigate flooding and landslides. It includes widening roads, stabilizing slopes using civil and bioengineering methods, enhancing drainage and bridge structures, and developing alternative escape routes. Rehabilitation efforts will involve pavement reconstruction and drainage improvements, supported by Performance-Based Maintenance Contracts and various consultancy services. Additionally, an electronic Project Management System will be implemented for real-time monitoring, alongside Road User Satisfaction Surveys and technical advisory support from academic institutions. The project will introduce a digital system for real-time inspection and monitoring of road works, alongside an institutional review to strengthen Assam’s Road Safety Lead Agency. Work zone safety will be integrated throughout, with an independent road safety audit ensuring best practices.The project aims to develop a green rural freight and public transportation system by establishing rural logistics hubs equipped with EV charging stations, solar-powered infrastructure, and amenities like workshops, refreshment areas, and transport bays. It includes a freight terminal linked to a district industrial park, demonstration ropeways for farm produce, and georeferenced transport stations with high-speed internet. Additional facilities include packaging, storage, sanitation, and roadside marketplaces. The project focuses on enhancing climate resilience and disaster preparedness in road infrastructure. It includes developing a climate adaptation framework/policy through multi-hazard risk analysis, integrating structural and bioengineering solutions into road design and maintenance. A Flood and Landslide Early Warning System (FLEWS) will be established to improve monitoring, forecasting, and communication with road users and communities, integrated into APWRD’s Road Asset Management System. Additionally, institutional capacity will be strengthened through the formulation of a robust transport emergency management and response plan to ensure rapid recovery after disasters.
projects.pdo: The proposed project development objective is to enhance the climate disaster resilience of hill roads and promote sustainable and inclusive development in hilly areas of Assam.

projects.project_abstract: The Gurugram Metro (Millennium City Center to Cyber City) focuses on enhancing urban public transport by developing the proposed Gurugram metro rail. It is the first project of a proposed Series of Project (SOP) developing a hierarchical and integrated transport system at three-levels to promote spatially balanced regional development and support Haryana's growth. The first level focuses on enhancing urban public transport in major cities starting from Gurugram Metro (from Millennium City Center to Cyber City) (SOP-1), integrated with expanded metro network and electric buses in (SOP-2), will also be supported by the World Bank (WB) under the Haryana Clean Air Project (P510686). The second level aims at improving regional connectivity between major economic hubs and their peripheral towns within a 150 km radius, as exemplified by the Delhi-SNB and Delhi Karnal regional rail corridors (SOP-3). The third level emphasizes the importance of intercity transport (SOP-4) to connect small-medium size cities with each other as well as with the major cities, with a significant role for buses to boost economic activities, facilitate access to jobs and services, and promote inclusive growth, by providing safe and accessible services to all, including vulnerable populations.The Gurugram Metro Rail project (SOP-1) consists of four components: Component 1: Develop a world-class metrorail system. This component will finance the construction of the elevated metro line in Gurugram to provide the backbone infrastructure of mass transit system in the city including i) In two packages, including the first civil works contract (viaduct structure of 15.5km and main structure of 14 stations) already under construction and financed by GMRL’s own funding  and the IBRD-financed second contract, consisting of viaducts structure of 13.5km, main structures of 13 stations, Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) and architectural finishing of all 27 stations. The stations will incorporate features of deploying solar panel to generate energy for use in the station, user friendly and inclusive station design and finishing, as well as climate resilient facilities against flooding and extreme heat; ii) Rolling stocks; and iii) Systems of traction and power supply, telecommunication, signaling, Automatic Fare Collection (AFC), lifts and escalators, digital system provides integrated services information (routes, fare, availability), and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC). Component 2: Maximize ridership and farebox revenues. This component will finance i) Multimodal Integration (MMI) infrastructure within the stations' within the stations’ right of way (RoW); and ii) First -Last Mile (FLM) services (through private sector, no additional project cost).Component 3: Capitalize of GMRL and project management. This component will support i) GMRL to utilize the resources provided under this component to increase the attractiveness to raise financing from DFIs and/or CBs through a sequenced financing approach; and ii) supporting GMRL in its daily operations, such as construction management, technical operations, procurement management, monitoring and evaluation, E&S compliance, and relevant areas to achieve the PDO.
projects.pdo: To (i) improve urban mobility and access to jobs in the Gurugram Metropolitan Area; and (ii) to ensure predictable, stable cashflows and effective performance monitoring of the metro rail system.

projects.project_abstract: The Bihar Rural Transformation Project (BRTP, P512959) is a INR 3000 crore (US$312.5M) operation, financed through an IBRD loan of INR 2100 crore (US$218.8M) and INR 900 crore (US$93.7M) in Government of Bihar counterpart funding. The Project Development Objective is to support more and better-paid jobs, and improve health and nutrition outcomes. Implemented by the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), popularly known as JEEViKA, the project builds on nearly two decades of World Bank engagement in Bihar and leverages JEEViKA's network of 10 million Self-Help Group members to drive a more ambitious agenda of market-oriented rural economic transformation.The project is structured around four components. Component A integrates smallholder producers into value chains through productive partnerships with private sector off-takers and builds an ecosystem of three million rural enterprises, with a focus on graduating enterprises from own-account to hired worker status. Component B  establishes three state-level apex institutions, a Marketing Federation, an Enterprise Anchor Facility, and a Shared Service Organization, and strengthens community institutions as platforms for health, nutrition, and climate resilience. Component C addresses financing and digital market failures through matching grants, a blended finance instrument, insurance products, and an AI-enabled Bihar Rural Stack. Component D covers project management, monitoring and evaluation, and knowledge partnerships. The project is expected to support approximately 773,000 more and better-paid jobs, benefit 3 million entrepreneurs, and reach 1.2 million women and 170,000 children through a community resilience and convergence model in 200 Cluster Level Federations.

projects.project_name: Unlocking Private Capital for Long-Term Infrastructure Financing and Bond-Market Transformation
projects.borrower: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development
projects.impagency: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development
projects.project_abstract: India faces a significant infrastructure financing gap, estimated at 4–5 percent of GDP annually, or roughly US$160 billion per year above current spending levels. While the government finances approximately 78 percent of existing infrastructure investment, this falls well short of the 8–10 percent of GDP required to meet long-term development goals through 2047. Two structural constraints drive this shortfall: a limited pipeline of bankable, well-prepared projects on the demand side, and an underdeveloped intermediation ecosystem on the supply side that prevents long-term domestic savings - held by pension funds, insurance companies, and provident funds - from being effectively deployed into infrastructure. Foreign participation remains similarly constrained by currency risk, limited hedging instruments, and the absence of credible borrowing histories among many Indian financial institutions active in the sector.To address these gaps, the Government of India established the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) in 2021 as a dedicated development finance institution with a mandate to mobilize private and institutional capital, deepen bond markets, and reduce the rating and risk perception barriers that limit investor participation. NaBFID's balance sheet alone cannot close the financing gap, but it is strategically positioned to act as a catalytic platform - particularly through partial credit enhancement mechanisms that can multiply its impact by unlocking large pools of domestic patient capital without proportionately expanding public sector balance-sheet exposure. Supportive regulatory action by the RBI in August 2025, including raising permissible credit enhancement coverage from 20 to 50 percent of bond value and standardizing instrument structures, has meaningfully strengthened the enabling environment for this approach.Project UPLIFT operationalizes this vision by supporting NaBFID in launching a Credit Enhancement Facility (CEF) that provides irrevocable, subordinated, contingent credit support to eligible infrastructure bond issuers, thereby elevating their credit ratings into investment-grade territory and broadening access to long-tenor institutional capital. The World Bank Group - through IBRD loans and guarantees, alongside a MIGA Non-Honoring of Financial Obligations guarantee and parallel ADB financing - backstops CEF exposures, lowers regulatory capital requirements, and supports access to international investors. This "One WBG" approach is designed to crowd in private domestic and foreign capital at scale, lower borrowing costs, and extend debt maturities in line with infrastructure asset lives, directly advancing India's growth agenda while operationalizing the Country Partnership Framework's leveraging bank model.
projects.pdo: To enhance access to long-term capital markets for infrastructure financing in India through NaBFID's credit enhancement facility.

projects.impagency: Department of Revenue (DM-Cell), Government of Himachal Pradesh; Directorate of Energy; Public Works Department; Jal Shakti Vibhag
projects.major_sector_name: Energy and Mineral Resources,Public Administration,Transportation,Water, Sanitation and Waste Management
projects.project_abstract: Cloudbursts, flash floods and landslide incidents triggered by heavy rain during the 2025 monsoon season (June to date) have caused extensive impacts in Himachal Pradesh, resulting in about 486 deaths and damages/losses estimated at US$653 million. Damages are primarily driven by impacts to the transport infrastructure, public buildings, power infrastructure, and water, sanitation and irrigation, while the livelihood sector additionally faces significant indirect losses due to disrupted access to markets, significant reduction of tourist arrivals etc. These events follow similarly devastating monsoon seasons in 2023 and 2024. These repeated extreme weather events have severely strained the state’s already constrained capacities, and substantial recovery needs from 2023 and 2024 remain unmet emphasizing the urgency of a speedy and resilient reconstruction and recovery effort. The proposed project will support the Government of Himachal Pradesh in advancing a resilient recovery process (transport corridors, public buildings, water/sanitation/irrigation schemes, and energy supply) while strengthening institutional capacities for disaster risk management, enhancing sectoral resilience for infrastructure sectors and supporting resilient livelihoods.
projects.pdo: To support resilient disaster recovery and livelihoods, and increase state capacities for risk-informed development.

projects.project_abstract: The proposed MPA Operation, MUWREP, will support the Government of Maharashtra in strengthening urban water supply and sanitation institutions, improving service delivery and wastewater reuse, and mobilizing private capital in participating cities. The Operation is designed as a hybrid PforR and IPF.  The Operation will support 35 urban local bodies across Maharashtra, covering large, medium, and smaller cities with varying institutional capacity, infrastructure needs, and financing readiness. The PforR will focus on large and medium municipal corporations, while the IPF component will support smaller municipal councils requiring integrated city-wide water and sanitation investments and implementation support. The Operation is expected to directly benefit more than 10 million people, with wider indirect benefits for over 30 million residents through improved governance, service delivery, wastewater management, and replicable financing models.The Program is organized around three pillars: strengthening institutions and policies for sustainable water supply, sanitation, and reuse; improving service delivery and resource efficiency through investments in water supply, sanitation, wastewater treatment, reuse, and renewable energy; and enhancing financial sustainability and access to private/commercial capital. Disbursement-linked indicators will incentivize state and city-level reforms, improved service outcomes, operational efficiency, financial performance, and private capital mobilization.A key feature of the Operation is its One World Bank Group blended financing approach, combining IBRD results-based financing, IFC investment and transaction advisory support, state and city contributions, commercial borrowing, pooled and municipal bonds, public-private partnerships, and land asset monetization. The Operation will support Maharashtra’s transition from infrastructure-led investments toward a more service-oriented, financially sustainable, and climate-resilient model for urban water supply and sanitation.
